overall.sentence: For the headline result, a layer-trimerized foliated Fibonacci phase and a stable foliated Laughlin phase found by exact diagonalization of up to 10 layers at nu = 1/3 per layer, there is no precedent found in the paper's references and 9 arXiv searches (2026-11-22); earlier work on infinite Laughlin/Halperin stacks (Refs. 34-40, 212, 213) is analytical and does not address energetics.

assessment.claim: 1: decoupled nu = 1/3 Laughlin stacks (foliated Laughlin phase) stay stable up to interlayer interactions comparable to intralayer ones, with a finite extrapolated gap
assessment.note: Wu and Zhang (cited [213]) and Ma et al. (cited [212]) treat infinitely stacked Laughlin/FQH layers and their 2D-to-3D transition with field theory; the question and system match, but ED of up to 10 layers with gap extrapolation is new in method.

assessment.claim: 2: in the bilayer, the interlayer pseudopotential V1(1) drives decoupled Laughlin -> Fibonacci, seen in overlaps, torus degeneracy and quasihole counting
assessment.note: Liu, Vaezi, Lee and Kim (cited [86]) already found the Fibonacci phase in the (330) bilayer driven by two-body interlayer couplings by ED and derived the bilayer exclusion rules; the paper presents this as agreement with [86], so no priority is claimed and no item is needed. The new parts are the CFT model wavefunction and the thin-torus pair-hopping mapping.

assessment.claim: 3: two-, three- and four-layer stacks host SU(3)_Nl topological order, with explicit CFT model wavefunctions and the spin-TQFT identified
assessment.note: Huang et al. (2025, not cited) study by numerics how interlayer coupling drives three decoupled Laughlin layers into a non-Abelian (Read-Rezayi Z3) state in trilayers; question and method are close, but their system is bosonic nu = 1/2 layers with tunneling, so fermionic nu = 1/3 layers with SU(3)_Nl order is new.

assessment.claim: 4: with NNN interlayer interactions the stack spontaneously trimerizes into a [1/3 1/3 0] layer charge pattern
assessment.note: No precedent found in the paper's references and 9 arXiv searches (2026-11-22); the only hits on layer symmetry breaking concern bilayer pseudospin ferromagnets and stripes. One query aimed at this claim failed (HTTP 429), so coverage is narrower than for the others.

assessment.claim: 5: within the trimerized sector the occupied pairs form Fibonacci bilayers, so a foliated Fibonacci phase exists in the 9-layer system
assessment.note: No precedent found in the paper's references and 9 arXiv searches (2026-11-22); the closest work is the isolated bilayer Fibonacci phase (one facet: question at the bilayer level only).

assessment.claim: 'To our knowledge, no numerical studies address the case of Nl > 4 layers.' (p. 3)
assessment.note: No numerical FQH study of more than four coupled layers turned up in the ED/DMRG multilayer query or the paper's references; the statement is hedged and holds as worded.

positioning: The paper sits between two literatures it cites well: analytical work on infinite stacks of Laughlin or Halperin layers and fracton field theories (Refs. 34-40, 212, 213), and ED of the 1/3 + 1/3 bilayer Fibonacci phase (Refs. 84-86). What it adds, as far as these searches show, is ED energetics for stacks of up to 10 layers, the SU(3)_Nl generalization with CFT wavefunctions, and a trimerized foliated Fibonacci phase, none of which an earlier paper found here addresses. The one uncited close paper is a 2025 study of trilayer bosonic Laughlin layers turning non-Abelian; a later preprint (2607.13127) on non-foliated 3D FQH phases in twisted multilayers appeared after this paper. Two of 11 arXiv queries failed with HTTP 429 after a retry; the failed foliated-FQH query was re-run in broader form, and the layer-CDW claim rests on one successful query.

issues.claim: Stacks of two, three and four coupled layers host non-Abelian SU(3)_Nl topological order, for which the paper builds explicit CFT model wavefunctions and identifies the spin-TQFT.
issues.headline: Uncited 2025 study of coupled Laughlin trilayers turning non-Abelian
issues.issue: Huang et al., arXiv:2509.17113 (2025), study numerically how interlayer coupling turns three decoupled Laughlin layers into a non-Abelian Read-Rezayi Z3 state, the trilayer analogue of the transition claimed here. Their layers are bosonic at nu = 1/2 and coupled mainly by tunneling, so the SU(3)_Nl result here is still new, but a referee who knows that paper will expect it to be cited and contrasted.

evidence.quote: We show that stacking ν = 1/3 Laughlin states yields a topological order with SU(3)Nℓ fusion rules, which we confirm numerically for Nℓ = 2, 3, 4.
evidence.location: Sec. I.C, Summary of the key results

issues.fix: Cite arXiv:2509.17113 where the multilayer non-Abelian results are introduced (Sec. I.B or I.C) and say in one sentence how this work differs: fermionic nu = 1/3 layers, interaction-driven without tunneling, SU(3)_Nl rather than Read-Rezayi order, and up to four layers.
